\[
\sigma_B^2(t) = \omega_0(t)\, \omega_1(t)\, \left(\mu_0(t) - \mu_1(t)\right)^2,
\quad
t^* = \arg\max_t \sigma_B^2(t),
\quad
I_{\text{out}} = \begin{cases} 255 & I > t^* \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(\omega_0, \omega_1\): The pixel counts at or below t, and above t
- \(\mu_0, \mu_1\): The mean levels of the two classes
- \(t^*\): The chosen threshold

Here omega_0 and mu_0 are the number and the mean of the pixels at or below level t. The values omega_1 and mu_1 are those of the pixels above it. Otsu showed that maximizing the between-class variance sigma_B^2 is the same as minimizing the variance within the two classes. Only the levels from the lowest to the highest one present are tried. Ties go to the smallest t, as in scikit-image and OpenCV. A flat image gets its own level as threshold and turns all 0. The result is 255 where the value is above the threshold and 0 elsewhere, or the reverse with Invert.
